Blue color and its themes:
The signs of Allah Almighty and the evidence of His power in the universe and the souls, the greatness of His creation, and the grace of Allah Almighty upon His servants and His benevolence to them.

Brown color and its themes:
Verses of the legal rulings.

Green color and its themes:
The traits of the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him), his attributes and honors; the believers and their attributes and their reward; and the Heaven and its descriptions.

Orange color and its themes:
The Day of Resurrection, its signs and preludes, warning people about it, about death, the grave, the reckoning, the resurrection, and the denial of the Judgment Day and the Resurrection.

Purple color and its themes:
The Holy Qur’an and its status, human characteristics, human's denial and arrogance, and the response to false accusations and allegations of the polytheists, and Allah’s law concerning his creation.

Red color and its themes:
Hell and its descriptions, and the torment of the polytheists and the disbelievers therein.

Yellow color and its themes:
The stories of the messengers and prophets, their biography and miracles, and the biography and stories of the previous nations.

Ordered after the “Mutun Talib al-Ilm” programme of the Prophet's Mosque (Sheikh Dr. Abdulmohsen Al-Qasim): start with level one, memorize a section, recite it from memory, then move on.
The best-known beginner's primer in Arabic grammar: speech, case endings and their signs, and the nominative, accusative and genitive.
A thousand verses on Arabic grammar and morphology — the summary of the science and the standard text to memorize.
Forty-two comprehensive hadith chosen by al-Nawawi as the foundations of the religion, completed to fifty by Ibn Rajab.
A short poem gathering the best-known categories and terms of hadith science — the student's gateway to the field.
Ibn Hajar's collection of the hadith used as evidence for fiqh rulings, arranged by the chapters of fiqh with their sources.
A famous admonition in verse in which al-Ilbiri urges his son to seek knowledge and not be deceived by this world.
What every reciter of the Quran must know: the articulation points and qualities of the letters, the rules of tajweed, stopping and the script.
An epistle establishing tawhid and answering the doubts raised against it, with a general and a detailed reply.
Chapters on singling out Allah in worship and on the shirk that opposes it and the paths to it, each proven with verses and hadith.
The ten matters that take a person out of Islam, briefly listed with their proofs so the Muslim can beware of them.
A compact text on hadith sciences that divides reports into their kinds and explains the accepted, the rejected and the causes of criticism.
Four principles that distinguish tawhid from shirk — a short epistle on the true meaning of the call of the messengers.
A poem on the law of inheritance: its causes and impediments, the heirs, fixed shares, residuaries and exclusion.
A concise treatise on the nine conditions, fourteen pillars and eight obligations of the prayer, with their proofs.
A statement of the creed of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah upon the way of the early imams, in short sentences easy to memorize.
A short poem on the rules of tajweed — noon sakinah and tanween, meem sakinah and the madd — usually the first text memorized in this science.
Hadith on legal rulings selected mostly from al-Bukhari and Muslim, arranged by the chapters of fiqh.
A poem rhyming in nun on wisdom and noble character, among the most celebrated verses of counsel.
The three questions every person is asked in the grave — who is your Lord, what is your religion, who is your Prophet ﷺ — answered with proofs from the Quran and Sunnah.
A few pages covering all of usul al-fiqh: rulings, command and prohibition, general and specific, abrogation, consensus, analogy and ijtihad.
The creed of Ahl al-Sunnah on Allah's names and attributes, the Last Day, predestination and the Companions, written by Ibn Taymiyyah for a judge from Wasit.
One of the best-known texts of Hanbali fiqh: al-Hajjawi's abridgement of al-Muqni' with added issues.

Learn to read the Quran step by step
Congratulations! You have completed the Qaida Nooraniyah.
Read words containing still letters smoothly, keeping qalqalah crisp mid-word.
Spell first, read joined second. Watch for the bounce in words like «يَقْطَعُ».
Read the doubled letter as two letters — still then moving — and hold the ghunnah on نّ and مّ two counts.
«أَبَّ» is أَبْ + بَ pressed together. On نّ and مّ, let the sound hum through the nose (ghunnah).
Read doubled letters inside Quranic words with full pressing and clear ghunnah.
Press firmly on every shaddah — rushing it is the most common mistake at this stage.
Read words that combine a doubled letter with a still letter without breaking the word apart.
Take the word in two halves, then join: «تَبْ + بَتْ = تَبَّتْ».
Read words carrying two doubled letters, giving each its full weight.
Slow right down: press the first shaddah completely before starting the second.
Distinguish the connected, separated and obligatory madd, and stretch each to its right length.
Hamzah after madd → stretch 4–5 counts. Shaddah after madd → stretch 6. Listen to a reciter and match the lengths.
Pronounce the laam of التعريف before moon letters, and merge it into sun letters.
The still laam: sun and moon letters
Moon: «الْقَمَر» — the laam is heard. Sun: «الشَّمْس» — the laam disappears into the shaddah. Compare the pairs aloud.
Stop correctly at the ends of words (still the last letter), then read complete surahs applying everything you have learned.
When stopping, the last vowel becomes sukoon: «نَسْتَعِينُ» is read «نَسْتَعِينْ». Crown your journey by reading Al-Fatihah aloud, slowly and beautifully.
Recognise every letter of the hijaa'iyah alphabet and say its full name from its correct articulation point (makhraj).
Point to each letter, listen, then repeat its name aloud three times. Do not move on until the letter's shape and name are inseparable.
Recognise each letter when it changes shape inside a word — first, middle and last position.
Spell each compound aloud letter by letter (التهجي), then pronounce it joined: «لام، مِيم — لم».
Read the disjoined letters that open some surahs by their letter names, exactly as recited.
These are read name by name: «الم» is read أَلِف لَام مِيم. Listen and echo the rhythm of each opening.
Pronounce every letter with each of the three short vowels, crisply and without stretching.
The short vowels: fathah, kasrah, dammah
Read each triple in one breath: «بَ بِ بُ». Keep the vowels short — a common beginner mistake is stretching them into madd.
Read tanween as a light noon sound at the end of the word: ً ٍ ٌ.
Tanween is simply a hidden noon: «بً» sounds like بَنْ. Read each triple like the vowels lesson, ending with the soft noon.
Read full words combining fathah, kasrah, dammah and tanween fluently, without spelling out.
First spell the word (التهجي), then read it joined. Repeat each word until it flows in one go.
Recognise the small alif, small yaa and small waw, and stretch them two counts like full madd letters.
The dagger alif «ٰ» works exactly like a written alif: «مَٰلِكِ» = «مَالِكِ». Stretch gently for two counts.
Stretch the madd letters (ا و ي) two counts, and glide softly through the leen letters (وْ يْ after fathah).
Madd: the letter before ا و ي carries the matching vowel — stretch two counts. Leen: «خَوْف، بَيْت» — glide, don't stretch.
Stop cleanly on a still letter, and let the qalqalah letters (ق ط ب ج د) bounce lightly.
Read the moving letter into the still one: «أَبْ». For ق ط ب ج د with sukoon, add the light echo of qalqalah.

Say Allahu Akbar and stand up for the second rak'ah. Repeat the same steps from Al-Fatiha to the second prostration, then sit for the tashahhud.

Sit as before and raise the index finger of your right hand while reciting the tashahhud. In a two-rak'ah prayer this is the final sitting. In a three- or four-rak'ah prayer, stand up after it and complete the remaining rak'ahs reciting only Al-Fatiha, then sit for the final tashahhud with the left foot tucked under the right shin and your seat on the ground (tawarruk).

All greetings, prayers and good things are for Allah. Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.
In the final sitting, after the tashahhud, send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ with the Ibrahimi salat. The supplication before the salam comes next.

O Allah, send prayers upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You sent prayers upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim; You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
Turn your head to the right saying As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullah, then to the left saying the same. Your prayer is complete.
Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.
Make sure you have wudu, your clothes and place are clean, the prayer time has begun, and you are facing the Qibla (the direction of the Kaaba). Intend the prayer in your heart.
Get ready and face the Qibla
Raise your hands to the level of your shoulders or ears with the palms facing the Qibla and say Allahu Akbar. The prayer has now begun.
Place your right hand over your left on your chest and look at the place of prostration. Then say the opening supplication (recommended, in the first rak'ah only).
Glory be to You, O Allah, and all praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You.
Standing with hands on the chest
Say A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim, then recite Surat Al-Fatiha. It is recited in every rak'ah. In the first two rak'ahs, recite another surah or a few verses after it.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path, the path of those You have blessed, not of those who earned Your anger, nor of those who went astray.
Say Allahu Akbar and bow, placing your hands on your knees with the fingers spread. Keep your back straight and level with your head. Say the tasbih three times.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most Great.
Rise from bowing while saying Sami' Allahu liman hamidah, raising your hands as in the opening takbir. Once you are standing upright, say Rabbana wa lakal-hamd.
Allah hears the one who praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs all praise.

Say Allahu Akbar and go down into prostration on seven parts: the forehead with the nose, both palms, both knees and the toes of both feet. Keep your elbows off the ground and away from your sides. Say the tasbih three times.
Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.
Say Allahu Akbar and sit up, resting on your left foot with the right foot upright and your hands on your thighs. Ask for forgiveness.
